article.title: Valve Funds Collabora's Port of Mesa's Open-Source RADV Vulkan Driver to Windows
article.summary: Collabora, sponsored by Valve, has an experimental Windows build of Mesa's open-source RADV Vulkan driver running Counter-Strike 2, though it isn't Vulkan-conformant yet.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

Collabora, the open-source engineering firm that maintains large parts of the Mesa graphics stack, has an experimental Windows build of RADV — Mesa's open-source Vulkan driver for AMD graphics hardware — running well enough to launch Counter-Strike 2, according to [Collabora](https://www.collabora.com/news-and-blog/news-and-events/cracking-windows-open-porting-radv-to-win32.html) and [Linuxiac](https://linuxiac.com/valve-backs-radv-vulkan-driver-port-to-windows/). Valve is sponsoring this phase of the work: "Thanks also to Valve for sponsoring this phase of our work to bring open drivers to Windows," Collabora engineer Louis-Francis Ratté-Boulianne wrote in a [company blog post](https://www.collabora.com/news-and-blog/news-and-events/cracking-windows-open-porting-radv-to-win32.html) published July 28, 2026.

## What We Know

- RADV is Mesa's open-source Vulkan driver for AMD graphics hardware and has become the de facto Vulkan driver for AMD GPUs on Linux, according to [Linuxiac](https://linuxiac.com/valve-backs-radv-vulkan-driver-port-to-windows/).
- Rather than porting AMD's Linux kernel driver to Windows, the project keeps RADV as a Windows user-mode Vulkan driver that talks to AMD's existing proprietary Windows kernel-mode driver, according to [Open Source For You](https://www.opensourceforu.com/2026/07/valve-funds-collabora-to-port-open-source-radv-vulkan-driver-to-windows/) and [Slashdot](https://news.slashdot.org/story/26/07/29/2140215/valve-sponsors-work-bringing-open-source-radv-driver-to-windows).
- This phase builds on earlier groundwork from developer Faith Ekstrand, who showed at XDC 2024 that Windows 10's WDDM2 interface offered "a much better foundation for a third-party driver" than prior approaches, according to [Collabora](https://www.collabora.com/news-and-blog/news-and-events/cracking-windows-open-porting-radv-to-win32.html).
- Because Windows' D3DKMT calls carry vendor-specific private data that ties AMD's user-mode and kernel-mode drivers together through an undocumented interface, Ekstrand built a tool called wddm2-pdd-re to log WDDM2 calls and reverse-engineer operations such as adapter queries, buffer allocation, queue creation, and command submission, according to [Collabora](https://www.collabora.com/news-and-blog/news-and-events/cracking-windows-open-porting-radv-to-win32.html) and [Open Source For You](https://www.opensourceforu.com/2026/07/valve-funds-collabora-to-port-open-source-radv-vulkan-driver-to-windows/).
- In this phase, Collabora removed the port's earlier dependency on the Windows Subsystem for Linux, reworked command-stream handling and synchronization, and "adds support for sparse bindings, tessellation, task shaders, and dynamic GPU capability detection," according to [Linuxiac](https://linuxiac.com/valve-backs-radv-vulkan-driver-port-to-windows/).
- With those changes in place, Counter-Strike 2 now launches on Windows through RADV "by starting the game with the -vulkan command-line argument," according to [Linuxiac](https://linuxiac.com/valve-backs-radv-vulkan-driver-port-to-windows/) — the first game reported running on the Windows port.
- Collabora frames the broader goal as enabling "a shared codebase across platforms, easier debugging and experimentation, faster turnaround on fixes," a description independently reported in the same words by [Slashdot](https://news.slashdot.org/story/26/07/29/2140215/valve-sponsors-work-bringing-open-source-radv-driver-to-windows) and [XDA Developers](https://www.xda-developers.com/as-linux-gaming-gains-ground-valve-brings-mesas-powerhouse-amd-driver-to-windows/).

## What We Don't Know

- The driver does not yet pass full Vulkan conformance tests, according to [Linuxiac](https://linuxiac.com/valve-backs-radv-vulkan-driver-port-to-windows/).
- Presentation on Windows still relies on a slower CPU-based path rather than native DXGI swapchains, and zero-copy presentation has not been implemented. Achieving it would require importing D3D12 images and could deliver "a 3x performance gain for applications that are not GPU-bound," according to [Collabora](https://www.collabora.com/news-and-blog/news-and-events/cracking-windows-open-porting-radv-to-win32.html).
- The most fundamental risk is that the port still depends on reverse-engineered knowledge of AMD's undocumented, private kernel-driver data structures, with no guarantee of compatibility from one driver version to the next — meaning a future AMD driver update could change those structures and break RADV on Windows without warning, according to [Collabora](https://www.collabora.com/news-and-blog/news-and-events/cracking-windows-open-porting-radv-to-win32.html) and [Open Source For You](https://www.opensourceforu.com/2026/07/valve-funds-collabora-to-port-open-source-radv-vulkan-driver-to-windows/).
- Collabora and outside reporting agree that lasting stability will require either a documented kernel interface from AMD or a maintained compatibility shim to absorb undocumented changes, according to [Slashdot](https://news.slashdot.org/story/26/07/29/2140215/valve-sponsors-work-bringing-open-source-radv-driver-to-windows) and [Open Source For You](https://www.opensourceforu.com/2026/07/valve-funds-collabora-to-port-open-source-radv-vulkan-driver-to-windows/).
- Neither Collabora nor Valve has said whether this Windows build of RADV is intended to ship as a supported end-user driver or remain a development and testing tool.

## Analysis

The project reflects Valve's long-running investment in the open-source Linux graphics stack that underpins SteamOS and the Steam Deck. A Windows-capable RADV would let Collabora and other Mesa contributors debug and extend one Vulkan driver codebase across both operating systems instead of maintaining separate mental models for AMD's proprietary Windows driver and RADV on Linux — the "shared codebase across platforms" argument Collabora makes in its blog post. For now, though, the driver remains a research prototype: it lacks Vulkan conformance, leans on a slower presentation path, and depends on reverse-engineered interfaces that AMD could change at any time. Whether it becomes a viable alternative to AMD's official Windows Vulkan driver depends on factors outside Collabora's control, chiefly whether AMD documents the kernel interface the port currently has to guess at.
